packs.title: Clay, Gardens and Coast
packs.promise: Explore Hoi An through distinct places and purposeful observations.

q.s: Collect three ways a model compresses architecture.
st: Pay ordinary park admission and follow the signed visitor path into the miniature-world area.
Choose three architectural models with different features: a roof, an opening and a support or tower.
For each, record one visible detail retained at small scale and one detail that seems simplified. Separate what you see from your guess about the maker’s decision.

q.s: Turn a vegetable garden’s rhythms into your own work.
st: From an admitted visitor path, observe a sequence of planted beds, path gaps and overhead frames or shade that is actually present.
Create a short visual score: use lines and spaces in a drawing, or five written phrases whose lengths follow the pattern you observed.
Add one change of pace for a gap, a darker bed or a turn in the path. Explain which garden feature prompted it. Work in a clear visitor position or finish afterward outside.

q.s: Collect evidence before making an archaeological guess.
st: Enter with the required museum ticket and find a glass-case group of pottery or burial vessels that is actually on view.
Collect one label fact, one visible shape or surface detail, and one question the objects do not answer for you.
Write a short interpretation linking your fact and detail, clearly separating the label’s information from your inference. Finish longer notes after leaving the room.

packs.title: Through the Ancient Town
packs.promise: Explore Hoi An through distinct places and purposeful observations.

q.s: Create two linked frames from Tan Ky’s visitor rooms.
st: Pay the required heritage entry and observe a dark timber-framed room beside a brighter opening that is actually visible on the visitor route.
Remember one line that continues between those spaces and one change in light. Leave the room without making a prolonged drawing or stationery session inside.

From a clear lawful public place afterward, create two linked frames in a drawing or written scene: one for the darker room, one for the brighter opening. Carry your observed line across both and explain the change.

q.s: Collect how Phung Hung’s facade separates street and house.
st: Find a public view of the whole timber front without standing in traffic, a shop doorway or the house’s threshold.
Collect a roof or eave line, an upper-gallery boundary and a lower opening that you can actually see.

Describe how those three layers change the relation between shelter, viewing outward and entering from the street. Record an interpretation as your own, rather than assigning a historic use to every opening.

q.s: Collect connections among the market’s everyday objects.
st: In open ordinary visitor aisles, choose a raw ingredient, a kitchen tool and a wrapper or container that you can see without handling merchandise.
Collect a practical detail of each: shape, material or how it is displayed. Ask a seller only if they are free and willing; a conversation is optional.
Propose a kitchen chain linking the three objects. Explain which connection you observed and which is your own possible use, without claiming a specific traditional recipe.
